data.narrative:
Aigen is a Series B robotics and manufacturing company founded by Kenny Lee and Richard Wurden, having raised approximately $23.7M to date. Valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of nine private companies and one public listing (277810.KQ), with three primary peers at the same stage: Generalist AI ($2.0B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), and Dexterity ($1.6B).

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.9x multiplier to the $23.7M raised as a proxy for post-money valuation, yielding $45M. The peer-median method uses valuations from three same-sector, same-stage comparables; the median of this set is $1.8B, with a range spanning $1.6B to $2.0B. This wide dispersion reflects meaningful valuation variance within the robotics cohort at this stage.

The triangulated analysis produces a range of $38M to $2.0B, with a median of $898M. The substantial gap between stage-progression ($45M) and peer-median ($1.8B) reflects the methodological tension inherent in valuing early-stage companies with limited capital history against later-stage peers. The peer-based approach likely overstates typical Series B positioning; stage-progression likely understates it. A defensible midpoint estimate would cluster in the $300M–$800M range, contingent on: Aigen's revenue trajectory and unit economics relative to named peers, the degree of capital intensity required for subsequent rounds, and whether the peer cohort commands sector-specific premium multiples. Key uncertainties remain Aigen's current run rate and competitive positioning within the robotics manufacturing vertical.
